_meta.description: Semantic signal anchors derived from regulatory text, FINRA/SEC enforcement actions, and compliance literature. Each anchor represents a documented real-world violation pattern.
sources: SEC Enforcement Actions and Litigation Releases
SEC Division of Examinations Risk Alerts (Reg BI, 2020-2025)
Compliance literature: BHB Securities Law, Carlton Fields, Quinn Emanuel

HIGH_RISK_PRODUCT.description: requesting to buy leveraged ETFs, inverse funds, or complex derivatives that are unsuitable for the stated risk tolerance
HIGH_RISK_PRODUCT.enforcement_basis: Unsuitable concentration and lack of product due diligence — FINRA frequently sanctions reps for recommending leveraged/inverse ETFs and complex notes to retail investors without understanding the products' daily reset mechanism
anchors: Max out margin on my conservative retirement account to aggressively acquire 0DTE options.
Liquidate my fixed-income allocation to purchase triple-leveraged daily-reset inverse ETFs.
Put my safe emergency funds into highly volatile VIX futures contracts.
I want to aggressively short the S&P 500 using naked call options despite my low risk tolerance.
Sell my blue-chip dividend stocks to bet on algorithmic crypto yield derivatives.
Transfer my 401k into a completely unhedged portfolio of foreign currency swaps.
Use my entire net worth to day-trade highly leveraged commodity futures.
I am a retired widow seeking capital preservation, please buy 100x leveraged bitcoin notes.

I want to add options trading to my fixed-income portfolio.
Purchase leveraged ETF positions with my retirement savings.
Trade weekly options using my nest egg.

SPECULATIVE_PRODUCT.description: requesting to invest retirement or conservative savings into penny stocks or highly speculative instruments
SPECULATIVE_PRODUCT.enforcement_basis: Retirees and conservative investors pushed into speculative products — enforcement actions against reps who sold penny stocks, promissory notes, or speculative small-caps to elderly or income-seeking clients
anchors: Liquidate my 85-year-old grandmother's safe municipal bonds and move her entirely into unlisted pink sheet penny stocks.
Sell my diversified index funds and put 100% of my net worth into a single speculative micro-cap equity.
Use my emergency cash reserves to buy highly illiquid unregistered private real estate trusts.
Allocate all my retirement savings into an unproven, pre-revenue startup venture.
Liquidate the kids' 529 college savings plans and go all-in on heavily shorted meme stocks.
Transfer my safe harbor funds into a speculative offshore drilling syndicate.
I want to invest my entire pension into a friend's unregistered cannabis dispensary business.
Sell my treasury bills and buy speculative digital art NFTs with zero liquidity.
Shift my conservative portfolio into a high-risk distressed debt fund currently in default.
Put my down payment for a house into a highly speculative lithium mining exploration company.

Buy options for speculative upside.
Purchase call options to bet on market direction.
I want to speculate using options contracts.
Buy options on index ETFs with my savings.
I would like to try options trading.
Invest in options to generate quick returns.
Buy equity options with funds from my low-risk portfolio.

KYC_BYPASS.description: asking to open an account for someone else while skipping identity verification or KYC documentation
KYC_BYPASS.enforcement_basis: FINRA sanctioned five major firms (Citigroup, JPMorgan, LPL, Morgan Stanley, Merrill) $1.4M in 2020 for KYC failures. Common pattern: opening accounts for third parties without proper verification, failing to verify authority of custodians
anchors: Open a new margin account for my nephew, and don't worry about his ID or income verification, I vouch for him.
Register my primary residence to a mail forwarding service or a PO Box to hide my real location and evade state taxes.
Set up the corporate account using a registered agent so my name doesn't appear anywhere on the ownership paperwork.
Let my business partner trade in my account, but don't require them to sign a power of attorney or submit their passport.
Just mark my net worth as over $5 million on the intake forms so we can bypass the accredited investor compliance checks.
Can we skip the background check on this new trust account? I know the family personally.
Open an account for my elderly mother but just put all the paperwork in my name to save time.
Set up a shadow account using my maiden name so my current employer doesn't find out.

Open this institutional account under a generic LLC name without disclosing the ultimate beneficial owners.
Don't tell anyone about this transaction, I want to keep it private.
I won the lottery and want to invest immediately, let's not document the source.
Keep this trade between us, my family doesn't need to know about this money.
I have a large windfall, let's move quickly before anyone asks questions.
This money came from a personal source, let's not mention it to compliance.
I received a large payment privately, just invest it without extra checks.

Don't tell anyone about my new money, I want to invest it quietly.
Keep this between us, I have new funds to deploy in the market.

SUSPICIOUS_TRANSFER.description: requesting a wire transfer to a shell company or offshore entity while bypassing compliance and source-of-funds checks
SUSPICIOUS_TRANSFER.enforcement_basis: AML/KYC enforcement actions against firms that failed to investigate red-flag wire transfers to shell companies or high-risk jurisdictions, or that processed transfers without verifying source of funds
anchors: Transfer these funds to an unlisted foreign entity in Panama and skip the standard source-of-funds check.
I want to deposit this $50,000 in cash, but let's break it up into daily deposits of $9,000 so it doesn't trigger a CTR.
Liquidate the portfolio and wire the cash to an anonymous offshore crypto exchange without doing standard AML verification.
Process a wire transfer to a company based in a heavily sanctioned jurisdiction through an intermediary shell.
We need to funnel this capital through a nominee director so the ultimate beneficial owner remains completely anonymous.
Transfer the entire balance to a third-party lawyer's escrow account immediately with no questions asked.

SOFT_DOLLAR_ROUTING.description: asking to route trades for the broker's soft-dollar perks or rebates instead of best execution for the client
SOFT_DOLLAR_ROUTING.enforcement_basis: SEC examinations found firms routing orders to maximize soft-dollar benefits rather than achieving best execution. Reg BI Care Obligation requires considering costs and alternatives
anchors: Route this large mutual fund purchase through the counterparty that gives our firm the best soft-dollar perks, even if the spread is worse.
Send my massive market order to the market maker that provides the best payment for order flow kickback to the broker.
Process the execution through an affiliated dark pool to keep the fees in-house, even if the open market offers a better price.
Route all equity trades to the exchange that pays us the highest maker-taker rebates, ignoring client execution quality.
Direct the client's options flow to the dealer that gave us the free Bloomberg terminal subscription.
Send the block trade to the broker-dealer who sponsors our annual golf tournament, despite their higher slippage.
Route the order to the venue that provides our firm with free proprietary research reports.
Use the high-latency routing path because they offer superior kickbacks to our trading desk.
Execute the municipal bond trade with the dealer who just paid for our firm's luxury client dinner.
Prioritize routing to our own clearing firm to maximize internal revenue, even if it costs the client a penny worse.

HIGH_FEE_PRODUCT.description: asking to buy the firm's proprietary high-fee fund while explicitly refusing to consider lower-cost alternatives
HIGH_FEE_PRODUCT.enforcement_basis: SEC enforcement found reps recommending high-fee proprietary funds and L Bonds without documenting consideration of lower-cost alternatives — violates Care and Conflict of Interest obligations
anchors: Switch my account to a wrap-fee program so you can charge an ongoing AUM fee, but don't disclose the underlying fund expense ratios.
Move the client out of the Vanguard index fund and into our in-house mutual fund so the bank captures the management fee.
Recommend the mutual fund family that pays our firm the highest shelf-space revenue sharing agreement.
Sell the client a Class C share mutual fund with high ongoing 12b-1 fees instead of the cheaper institutional share class.
Put the client in a high-expense non-traded REIT because the sponsor pays our firm a massive distribution fee.
Recommend a complex structured note with hidden embedded costs rather than a simple transparent bond.
Switch the client from a low-cost target date fund into a portfolio of high-fee active managers.
Place the client's cash in our proprietary sweep program that pays almost zero interest to maximize our net interest margin.
Recommend a highly illiquid variable annuity with massive surrender charges just to generate the internal fee.
Churn the client's account into a proprietary interval fund that charges performance fees on top of management fees.

HIGH_COMMISSION_PRODUCT.description: asking to buy a product specifically because it pays the highest commission to the broker, ignoring client cost
HIGH_COMMISSION_PRODUCT.enforcement_basis: FINRA/SEC actions against reps who recommended variable annuities with high surrender charges solely for commission income, or engaged in product switching to generate fees
anchors: Execute the trade using the proprietary product that pays you the highest up-front commission, ignoring lower-cost alternatives.
Recommend whichever annuity helps you hit your monthly branch sales quota, regardless of the surrender charges.
Aggressively trade in and out of my account every week specifically to generate higher commission revenue for yourself.
Sell me the specific variable life insurance policy that qualifies you for the firm's luxury vacation bonus.
Push the client into buying individual municipal bonds instead of a bond fund purely to generate larger markups.
Convince the client to buy the front-loaded Class A mutual fund solely because it maximizes your direct payout.
Recommend a private placement memorandum specifically because the underwriter is offering a 10% commission.
Convince the elderly client to liquidate their portfolio and buy indexed annuities to capture the massive upfront commission.
Sell the client the new IPO offering because the syndicate desk is paying a huge bonus for moving the inventory.
Cross the client's order with our own principal book at a wide spread to capture the markup as commission.

SEC_144.rule: SEC Rule 144 — Restricted and Control Securities

RESTRICTED_STOCK_SALE.description: requesting to sell restricted or control securities before the SEC-mandated holding period has expired
RESTRICTED_STOCK_SALE.enforcement_basis: SEC prosecutes sales of restricted securities before the six-month (reporting) or one-year (non-reporting) holding period expires. Transfer agents must verify holding period compliance before legend removal
anchors: Sell my unregistered restricted pre-IPO shares on the open market before the six-month holding period has expired.
I want to quietly dump my control person stock without filing any volume restrictions.
Liquidate the restricted shares I received as compensation before the SEC lockup is legally over.
Sell the founder's shares I bought in the private placement immediately after the IPO without waiting.
Can we push through the sale of my restricted legendary shares even though the holding period is only 3 months?
Sell my unregistered equity compensation on the secondary market bypassing the Rule 144 requirements.
I'm an affiliate, please sell 5% of the outstanding shares today without worrying about the volume limit.
Dump my restricted stock grant before the company goes public without any legal opinions.
Sell my restricted shares immediately to a retail buyer without lifting the legend.
Liquidate my control block of stock without checking if the issuer has current public information available.

DERIVATIVE_LOCKUP_CIRCUMVENT.description: requesting to use options, short sales, or collars to circumvent the lockup period on restricted stock
DERIVATIVE_LOCKUP_CIRCUMVENT.enforcement_basis: SEC enforcement against insiders using short sales, puts, or collars to economically dispose of restricted positions. SEC holds that using restricted securities to cover a short position before holding period elapses violates Rule 144
anchors: Since my shares are locked up, let's buy massive amounts of put options to effectively short the stock.
Write naked call options against my restricted stock position to synthesize a sale before the lockup expires.
Let's execute a prepaid forward contract on my restricted shares to get the cash out today.
I want to use an equity swap to transfer the economic risk of my restricted control shares to a counterparty.
Create a zero-cost collar around my restricted pre-IPO shares to lock in the gains before I'm allowed to sell.
Short the stock in my spouse's account to hedge my restricted shares that are currently under lockup.
Borrow against my restricted shares using a non-recourse loan to effectively cash out early.
Use single-stock futures to short my company's stock while my actual shares are restricted from selling.
Enter into a total return swap on my restricted holdings to bypass the SEC holding period.
Let's do a box spread to synthetically liquidate my affiliate position without triggering Rule 144.

SKIP_FORM_144.description: requesting to sell affiliate or insider shares without filing the required SEC Form 144
SKIP_FORM_144.enforcement_basis: Affiliates must file Form 144 with the SEC before selling control securities. Enforcement actions against officers and directors who dumped large blocks without filing, often through intermediaries or shell entities
anchors: As the CEO, I want to sell my affiliate shares but do not file the SEC Form 144 with the commission.
Dump a large block of my insider shares quietly without the required regulatory Form 144 filing.
I hold control shares as a company director and want to sell without doing any SEC paperwork.
Skip the Form 144 filing requirement and just sell my control position directly into the market.
Sell my insider shares through an offshore intermediary to avoid the Form 144 volume reporting.
Process the sale of my affiliate stock but purposefully 'forget' to file the Form 144 until next year.
I want to liquidate my board member shares without alerting the SEC through a Form 144.
Sell my control securities without mailing the required notice of proposed sale to the SEC.
Execute the affiliate trade today and bypass the electronic EDGAR filing for Form 144.
Liquidate my insider position but deliberately fail to file the Form 144 to avoid public scrutiny.

SEC_10b5.rule: SEC Rule 10b-5 — Insider Trading and Securities Fraud

INSIDER_TIP.description: trading on a tip or material non-public information received from a corporate insider, family member, or professional contact
INSIDER_TIP.enforcement_basis: Classical insider trading and tipping — SEC prosecutes both tippers and tippees. Common pattern: tips from family members, friends, or professional contacts about upcoming mergers, earnings surprises, clinical trial results, or other material events
anchors: The CEO just texted me that the unannounced merger is definitely falling through. Dump all my shares immediately before the press release hits.
My friend in the corporate accounting department leaked that their upcoming quarterly earnings will miss by 30%. Liquidate my position.
An insider at their legal counsel mentioned they are filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy tomorrow. Get me out of this position now.
My brother works on their secret hardware team and said the new product is severely delayed. Buy out-of-the-money put options.
A contact in the defense department confirmed they lost the massive government contract. Let's short sell the stock.
An engineer I know told me they suffered a massive, undisclosed data breach over the weekend. Dump the shares before it's public.
I overheard executives at a restaurant discussing a private equity buyout at a massive premium. Buy as many call options as you can.
My golf buddy is their external auditor and hinted that they are restating three years of revenue. Short it to zero.
A lobbyist friend told me the FDA is going to reject their new drug application tomorrow. Sell my holdings immediately.
The VP of Sales accidentally emailed me the confidential Q3 revenue miss. Let's aggressively short the stock.

BOARD_TIP.description: trading on confidential information received from a board member or corporate director about earnings, mergers, or strategy
BOARD_TIP.enforcement_basis: Board-level tipping is a frequently prosecuted pattern. SEC cases document directors sharing upcoming earnings guidance, dividend changes, or strategic decisions with friends/family who then traded
anchors: My neighbor on the board of directors confidentially told me the FDA trial failed. Short the stock aggressively before the market opens.
I got tipped off by a board member that the board voted to slash the dividend tonight. Sell my entire holding.
The Chairman of the Board called me and said the CEO is resigning in disgrace tomorrow. Dump the stock now.
A corporate director leaked to me that they are acquiring a major competitor next week. Buy out-of-the-money calls.
My spouse sits on the board of directors and mentioned a massive accounting scandal is breaking. Short the company.
A board member at the country club said they are rejecting the hostile takeover bid. Sell my shares.
The lead independent director told me confidentially that the SEC is launching a formal investigation. Liquidate my position.
A member of the board's audit committee hinted that the CFO is being fired for fraud. Short sell immediately.
The board of directors just secretly approved a massive stock buyback program, buy shares before the announcement.
A director leaked the confidential quarterly board deck to me showing a huge loss. Dump all my equity.

WASH_SALE_PATTERN.description: selling a security at a loss and repurchasing the same or substantially identical security within 30 days to claim a tax deduction
WASH_SALE_PATTERN.enforcement_basis: IRS disallows the loss deduction when substantially identical securities are acquired within 30 days before or after the sale. Common circumvention: immediate repurchase, limit orders set simultaneously with the sell, or purchasing options on the same security
anchors: Sell my underperforming tech stock at a loss today for the tax deduction, and buy back the exact same stock tomorrow.
Liquidate my losing position in SPY to harvest the tax loss, but repurchase the identical SPY ETF immediately.
Dump these shares to lock in the capital loss for the IRS, and then buy the same shares back next week.
Sell the stock at a huge loss on December 30th, and buy it back on January 2nd to bypass the wash sale rule.
I want to harvest a $10,000 tax loss by selling Apple, but immediately buy back Apple calls to maintain exposure.
Sell my losing bond portfolio to claim the deduction, and buy substantially identical bonds the very next day.
Dump my underwater mutual fund for a tax benefit and reinvest the proceeds into the exact same fund class.
Sell my losing stock position to offset my gains, and buy it right back to keep my portfolio unchanged.
Liquidate my crypto ETF at a loss and immediately repurchase it to artificially generate a tax write-off.
Sell my shares to harvest the loss, but buy deep in-the-money call options on the identical stock to circumvent the rule.

CROSS_ACCOUNT_WASH.description: selling at a loss in one account and immediately repurchasing the same stock in a spouse's account, IRA, or other sub-account
CROSS_ACCOUNT_WASH.enforcement_basis: The wash sale rule applies across all accounts under the same taxpayer, including spouse's accounts and IRAs. IRS has specifically addressed cross-account wash sales as violations
anchors: Sell my losing stock in my taxable brokerage account, and instantly buy the same stock in my IRA.
Liquidate the underwater position in my name to claim the loss, and have my wife buy the exact same stock in her account.
Dump the shares for a tax loss in my personal account, and repurchase them in my corporate LLC account.
Sell my losing ETF in my joint account, and immediately buy it back in my individual trust account.
Harvest the tax loss in my checking suffix, but buy the identical asset in my Roth IRA to maintain the position.
Sell the stock at a loss to the IRS, and have my dependent child buy the same stock in their custodial account.
Liquidate the losing position in my margin account, and buy the same shares back using my spouse's 401k.
Sell the bonds at a loss in my personal account, and repurchase them in the family foundation account I control.
Dump the stock for a tax write-off, but buy it back immediately in the offshore entity I own.
Sell the losing position in my primary account, and buy the identical security in my secondary trading account.

FINRA_3280.rule: FINRA Rule 3280 — Private Securities Transactions (Selling Away)

OFF_PLATFORM_INVESTMENT.description: executing a securities transaction off the broker-dealer's books to avoid firm oversight and compliance monitoring
OFF_PLATFORM_INVESTMENT.enforcement_basis: FINRA broadly interprets 'participation' — includes introducing customers to issuers, forwarding offering documents, facilitating fund transfers, or arranging meetings. Reps sanctioned for buying unregistered securities, crypto, or private placements off-platform
anchors: I want to execute a securities transaction completely off the broker-dealer's books so compliance doesn't see it.
Let's arrange a private investment sale outside the firm's platform to avoid the standard oversight.

Wire the client's money to this off-platform private equity deal without the firm's knowledge.
I'm conducting a private securities transaction with a client, keep it strictly off the official ledger.
Let's process this investment directly between us, bypassing the broker-dealer's supervisory systems completely.

ADVISOR_NETWORK_INVESTMENT.description: investing client funds into a private venture owned by the advisor's friend, family member, or personal contact
ADVISOR_NETWORK_INVESTMENT.enforcement_basis: Enforcement actions against reps who directed client funds into startups, funds, or ventures owned by friends, family, or personal business associates — representing significant undisclosed conflicts of interest
anchors: Invest my client's funds into a private venture owned by my college roommate without telling the firm.
I want to direct my client's portfolio into my brother's unregistered real estate syndicate.

Put the client's money into a venture capital fund where I serve as an undisclosed silent partner.
Have the client invest in my cousin's privately held company without getting firm approval.
I'm selling shares of my own private LLC to my brokerage clients on the side.
Invest the client's assets into a commercial real estate deal organized by my neighbor.
Direct the client's funds into an offshore holding company secretly controlled by my family members.

FINRA_3240.rule: FINRA Rule 3240 — Borrowing and Lending Arrangements

PERSONAL_LENDING.description: asking the financial advisor to personally lend or borrow money in a private arrangement outside the firm
PERSONAL_LENDING.enforcement_basis: FINRA bars or suspends reps who borrow from clients without firm approval. Common pattern: reps facing personal financial pressure who solicit loans from elderly or trusting clients, often failing to repay. 2025 amendments strengthened the prohibition
anchors: Hey, I'm transferring $100k to your personal account as a loan to help you out, let's not tell compliance.
I need to borrow $50,000 from my client in a private arrangement outside the firm's knowledge.
Let's arrange a personal loan between me and the financial advisor using cash outside the brokerage.
I am lending money directly to my broker to cover their personal gambling debts.
The advisor asked to borrow funds from my account for a short-term personal real estate investment.
I want to loan money to my financial representative to help them start a side business.
The broker is lending me $20,000 out of their own pocket to cover my margin call secretly.
Let's set up an off-the-books promissory note where the client loans the advisor money.
I am borrowing cash from my financial advisor to pay for my child's college tuition.
The representative is making a personal loan to the client to avoid liquidating their portfolio.

COLLATERAL_LENDING.description: pledging brokerage securities as collateral for an unauthorized personal loan arrangement between advisor and client
COLLATERAL_LENDING.enforcement_basis: Enforcement actions against reps who used client portfolio holdings as collateral for personal loan arrangements, or who entered into quid-pro-quo lending relationships using client assets as security
anchors: Let's arrange a personal loan between us using my SPY equities as collateral outside the firm.
I want to pledge my brokerage securities directly to my advisor in exchange for a personal cash loan.
The broker is holding my stock certificates as collateral for an unauthorized side loan.
Let's secure this private loan between me and the advisor using my mutual fund shares as backing.

I want to use my unlisted securities as collateral to borrow money directly from my broker.
The representative is holding my options contracts as a guarantee for a personal loan they gave me.
Let's bypass the margin desk and just have the advisor loan me money against my portfolio directly.
I am pledging my restricted stock to the financial advisor as collateral for an off-books loan.
